title: Can the Minkowski class number bound for algebraic number fields be derived from the geometry-of-numbers framework

problemStatement.formal: For a number field K, record the Mathlib class-group finiteness consequences of the Minkowski class number bound, including positivity of classNumber K and the class-number-one PID criterion.
problemStatement.plain: Document how Mathlib packages the geometry-of-numbers route to finite class groups: Minkowski bounds give finite class groups, positive class numbers, and the PID criterion for class number one.
whyMatters: Minkowski's class number bound is the bridge from convex geometry to arithmetic finiteness of ideal classes.
The class-number-one criterion is a standard way to recognize when the ring of integers is a PID.
The rational-number-field example provides a concrete sanity check for the abstract number-field API.

proven: The class group of the ring of integers of any number field is finite by Mathlib instance search (Lean: classGroup_finite).
The class number of any number field is positive (Lean: classNumber_pos).
Class number one is equivalent to the ring of integers being a principal ideal ring (Lean: classNumber_one_iff_PID).
The rational number field has class number one (Lean: rat_classNumber_eq_one).
The ring of integers of Q is a principal ideal ring as a consequence (Lean: rat_integers_isPID).
knownResults.goal: Expose the verified class-group finiteness and class-number consequences supplied by Mathlib's Minkowski-bound development.
